subject.title: fix(msteams): bound SSO API JSON response reads to prevent OOM

question: Should this SSO hardening land only after OpenClaw owns or proves a bounded read on the SDK-backed Microsoft Teams sign-in route?
rationale: The patch changes an availability/security boundary, but current production sign-in invokes delegate to SDK handlers rather than the helper this PR changes.

options.title: Retarget the live SSO route
options.body: Require the cap and route-level proof to cover the SDK-backed `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` path before merge.

options.title: Accept SDK ownership with proof
options.body: Allow the helper-only change only if maintainers get concrete dependency proof that the Teams SDK already enforces an equivalent response cap.

options.title: Pause helper-only hardening
options.body: If the manual helper is no longer a production path, close or replace this PR instead of merging tests for an unused route.

recommendation.title: Retarget the live SSO route
recommendation.body: Require the cap and route-level proof to cover the SDK-backed `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` path before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest recent routing candidate for the monitor/SDK-adapter boundary now used by production sign-in invokes.
